card.What will I do: Your first day in the Group GRC Office. Complete onboarding: confirm your assignment, accept the conduct rules, set your hours and make your first recorded submission.
card.Why am I doing this: Every GRC job starts with conduct: you handle other people's data and you produce records that auditors rely on. Before you touch any task, the organisation needs proof that you know the rules (BKB-POL-024 §6.1) and that your workspace records your work correctly.
What will I learn: Follow the mentee conduct and data rules — synthetic data only, own work, no AI tools for task work — see BKB-POL-024 §3.1; BKB-POL-022 §7.1
Recognise what a controlled record looks like: hash, UTC time, version, naming convention — see Capture standard — BKB-MEN-101 §9
Use the scripted help: the "In simpler words" note on every step, the glossary and the "Report a problem" form — see Guided Model — principle G7
Plan your own working hours so that reminders and task messages reach you — see Guided Model — "My schedule"

See which areas of the GRC capability this task practises — U3 Culture and conduct; D1 Mandate, leadership and resources; O6 Speak-up channels and investigation — and what your deliverables evidence — see Ref-Capability map (Learn › Reference pages)
card.How to do it: 6 numbered steps, of which 3 are decisions from options (judgement share 50 %). Rules you will use: copy and calculation only (Learn › Rule tables). Assigned by the Cybersecurity Program Manager, who has written the "In simpler words" note on every step. Help is pre-written on the platform (no live chat).
What to read or refer: BKB-POL-024 — §3.1 policy statements; §6.1 Procedure: Mentee onboarding
BKB-POL-022 — §7.1 Guideline: Using generative AI safely (no AI tool is used for task work)
BKB Group GRC Charter — §10 and §10.1 Rules of engagement for mentees

Ref-Capability map — rows for F1.1 — the capability areas this task practises (U3 Culture and conduct; D1 Mandate, leadership and resources; O6 Speak-up channels and investigation) and what your deliverables evidence
card.Where to add: Platform: Home › My Tasks; Policies › Onboarding attestations. Template: Platform forms (ADM-UND, ADM-RULES, SCHED) (issued in /M2610-00001/W01/F1.1/01_Inputs). Submit to /M2610-00001/W01/F1.1/03_Submission. GRC record: Your admin folder /M2610-00001/00_Admin.
What to deliver: SCHED — My working hours (Platform schedule form)
card.Why is this important: Without a signed undertaking your account is not opened for data (BKB-POL-024 §6.1 step 3). A confirmed conduct breach later is an automatic fail (BKB-MEN-101 §13.2 gates). The manifest you test here is the same mechanism that makes every later submission auditable. Feeds: every task (ADM-RULES).

steps.t: Open Home › My Organisation

"My Organisation" is your assignment: the two organisations you support, their offices, the person (role) who assigns each task and your start date. You will see these names in every task. Nothing to decide here — read, then tick the step.

steps.t: Decide: A colleague asks for your login so they can finish a step f…
steps.w: DECIDE: A colleague asks for your login so they can finish a step for you while you are offline. What do you do? Options: A) Share it but change the password later  B) Share it just for today  C) Refuse and tell the programme office with "Report a problem". Choose one. After you submit, you see why each option is right or wrong. Then: Open "Undertaking" (Policies › Onboarding attestations). Read it. Sign it (ADM-UND).
opt: Share it but change the password later
Refuse and tell the programme office with "Report a problem"
steps.why: Accounts are personal. Sharing breaks the undertaking and makes the work not yours (BKB-POL-024 §3.1).
steps.help: First a scripted question with three options. Think about who owns your account. Choose one option; the platform shows the best option and why after you submit the task. Then open the undertaking, read it and sign it — your signature is the record that you know the rules.

steps.t: Decide: You do not understand a rule. What do you use
steps.w: DECIDE: You do not understand a rule. What do you use? Options: A) The "In simpler words" note on the step and the glossary in Learn  B) Any public chatbot, pasting the task text  C) A friend's paid AI account. Choose one. After you submit, you see why each option is right or wrong. Then: Open "Data rules". Tick each box (ADM-RULES).
opt: The "In simpler words" note on the step and the glossary in Learn
Any public chatbot, pasting the task text
steps.why: All help is scripted on the platform. No AI tool is used for task work, and work data never leaves the platform (BKB-POL-022 §7.1).
steps.help: Again one scripted question. The point: all help on this platform is pre-written — the note you are reading now, the glossary in Learn, the rule tables under Learn › Rule tables. No AI tool and no chat is used for task work. Then tick every box of the data rules.

steps.t: Decide: You can work 15 hours a week
steps.w: DECIDE: You can work 15 hours a week. Which schedule meets the programme rules (≥ 12 h, ≥ 3 days, ≤ 4 h per window)? Options: A) One 15-hour day on Saturday  B) Two days of 6 hours  C) Monday–Thursday, 3 h 45 min each day. Choose one. After you submit, you see why each option is right or wrong. Then: Open "My schedule". Select your start and end times for each weekday you will work. Minimum 12 hours a week, on at least 3 days. Click "Save" (SCHED).
steps.why: Only option A uses at least 3 days and keeps every window at 4 hours or less.
steps.help: Choose the schedule that follows the three numbers: at least 12 hours a week, on at least 3 days, never more than 4 hours in one sitting. Then enter your own hours in "My schedule" — reminders and task messages arrive only inside those hours.

steps.t: Open the file READ-ME-FIRST in your task folder (01_Inputs)
steps.w: Open the file READ-ME-FIRST in your task folder (01_Inputs). Add your name and mentee ID where it says so. Save it to 02_Working and click "Submit". Check that the receipt shows a hash and a UTC time — every deliverable you submit is recorded this way.
steps.o: Manifest with hash and UTC time
steps.help: Your first real submission, the way every deliverable works: a file goes from 01_Inputs (what you receive) through 02_Working (your work) to Submit. The receipt shows a hash (a fingerprint of the file) and a UTC time. If the hash is missing, use "Report a problem".

steps.t: Open "My plan"
steps.w: Open "My plan". All your due dates for the 12 weeks are already set. Click "Done".
steps.help: "My plan" lists every due date of the 12 weeks. The system set them inside your working hours. You do not change anything — this step only shows you where to look. Then click "Done".

Phishing and business-email compromise leading to credential theft or fraudulent payment
Enforce dual approval and out-of-band verification for bank-detail changes; quarterly localised phishing simulations; conditional-access policies.
Personal-data breach through misconfigured cloud / SaaS services
Continuous CSPM with 7-day SLA for critical findings; SaaS security posture review of top-10 SaaS holding personal data; quarterly access recertification.
Failure to meet statutory breach-notification deadlines in Philippines
Embed country notification clocks in the incident tool with automated timers; run a notification drill per office annually; pre-approved regulator templates in local language.
Compromise or failure of a critical SaaS / cloud supplier
Tier suppliers by criticality; continuous monitoring of Critical suppliers; documented exit plans and tested alternate providers for Mission Critical SaaS.
Misuse of privileged access by insiders or compromised administrators
Just-in-time privileged access with session recording for Tier 4 systems; UEBA alerts on anomalous bulk access; segregation of duties review.
Weekly external attack-surface scanning; 48–72h SLA for KEV-listed vulnerabilities; virtual patching where fixes are unavailable.
DDoS and hacktivist campaigns against public-facing services
Contract always-on DDoS mitigation with scrubbing capacity; run DDoS response exercise; monitor hacktivist channels via CTI.
Threat-hunting programme focused on relevant APT TTPs; egress monitoring and DLP for Tier 4; compromise assessment annually.
Natural hazard disrupting the Manila office (Typhoon)
Validate office BCP against local hazard scenario; ensure on-prem Mission Critical systems have out-of-region DR; staff safety and communication cascade tested.
Failure of local power, telecom or internet infrastructure
Dual diverse ISPs and SD-WAN; generator fuel contracts sized to 72h; failover of office-dependent services to cloud or another office.
Geopolitical instability, sanctions or civil unrest affecting operations
Maintain country crisis plan with evacuation and remote-operation options; monitor sanctions regimes; scenario-plan data-access restrictions.
Assign regulatory-change owner for the office; 30-day impact-assessment SLA; subscribe to regulator alerts and local counsel updates.
Bribery, corruption or weak contract enforceability
Anti-bribery training for regional leadership; due diligence of agents and intermediaries; gifts & hospitality register reviewed quarterly.
Loss of key security / compliance staff and skills shortage
Document control ownership and deputies; cross-train using GRC Task Libraries; use GRC 101 mentees for Tier-1 activities under supervision.

The alignment below means a GRC 101 graduate has practised every Lead Implementer competency on the synthetic BKB organisations and can sit a Lead Implementer course and exam with a strong foundation. It does not award, replace or guarantee any certification. The PECB "Lead Implementer" credential additionally requires 5 years of professional experience (2 in information security management) and 300 hours of ISMS project activity; "Provisional Implementer" requires the exam only. Statements are summarised from the PECB handbook; ISO text is not reproduced. R01: Ask in this order and stop at the first "yes": 1) Made by a parliament or a regulator? → Law / regulation. 2) Can an organisation get a certificate? → Certifiable standard. 3) Is the result an auditor's report on controls? → Attestation framework. 4) Is it contract wording? → Model contract. 5) Otherwise → Voluntary framework.
R02: A standard applies to an office when the addendum §2 row for that office names it, or the addendum §3 says "all offices". Copy the office names. Do not add offices.
R03: Take the three obligations for the office with the shortest deadline in addendum §2 (hours before days). If there are fewer than three, add mandatory standards in the order of addendum §3.
R04: Copy the first five parties listed in addendum §4, in the same order, with the requirement written next to each.
R05: Walk the BKB-STD-001 §5 decision tree from Q1. Then apply BKB-POL-004 §3.1: personal data, children's data and credentials are never below Tier 3; aggregated data takes the highest tier of its parts; derived outputs take the tier of the source.
R06: Write: "Because of <cause>, <event> may occur, leading to <consequence> for <asset>." Copy the words for cause, event and consequence from the scenario facts. Copy the asset name from the register.
R07: Find the likelihood and impact descriptor in the ERM scale table (BKB-ERM-001 §6.2–6.4) that uses the same words as the facts. Write the descriptor number. Residual likelihood = inherent likelihood − 1 for each existing control marked "working" (lowest value 1). Residual impact = inherent impact. Score = likelihood × impact. Rating: 1–5 Low, 6–11 Medium, 12–19 High, 20–25 Critical.
R08: LOW-criticality appetite = 11. Residual score ≤ 11 → Decision "Accept and monitor". Residual score > 11 → Decision "Treat"; due days from BKB-ERM-001 §7: Critical 30, High 90, Medium 180.
R09: Check D1 to D10 in order (Ref-Defect codes). If any check fails → Reject and write every failed code. If none fails → Accept. If D9 fails, also click "Report data issue" and do not copy the content.
R10: If a sentence has two actions (joined by "and" or ";"), make two rows. Owner role = the owner of the linked BKB policy in the BKB-POL-000 index.
R11: Full = a BKB policy clause AND a procedure AND an Annex A control exist. Partial = only one or two of the three exist. None = none exists.
R12: Write: "Missing: <policy clause / procedure / control>. Owner: <policy owner>."
R13: Covered = a clause has the same action AND the same time limit. Partly = the action is there but the time limit or owner is missing. Not covered = no clause. Where to fix: requirement names a country or office → Addendum; otherwise → Group policy. Redline frame: "<Role> shall <action> within <time limit>." Never make a Group value weaker; if it would, write "Exception needed".
R14: Use the six fixed steps: 1 Trigger received → 2 Check input → 3 Do the action → 4 Record → 5 Tell the owner → 6 Exception: escalate. For each step copy the responsible role and the time limit from the addendum §5 or the policy clause shown on your task page. Do not invent numbers.
R15: Look up the control frequency in Ref-Sampling and copy the minimum sample. Select the sample with the random seed shown on your task page (the platform does the selection when you click "Select sample").
R16: Fieldwork starts 30 days after the end of the audit period. Due date = fieldwork start − 5 working days.
R17: Copy for every request: "The evidence must be dated, show who produced it, cover the whole period and be an unchanged system export."
R18: A control has a gap when it has fewer than 2 accepted files. For each gap write: "Please send 2 more files for <control> covering <period> by <due date>."
R19: Effective: no exceptions. Effective with exceptions: only Low/Medium exceptions and ≤ 5 % of the population. Not effective: any High exception or > 5 %. Control tests (T8.2): 1–2 deviations = effective with exceptions; > 2 = not effective.
R20: Copy the action for the exception type from Ref-Actions (e.g., U1 active leaver account → "Disable within 1 working day; check for use after termination" — owner IAM team).
R21: Voluntary leaver: account disabled within 4 hours of termination. Involuntary leaver: within 1 hour. KPI = leavers fully disabled within SLA ÷ all leavers × 100.
R22: One change-log row for each changed field: row ID, field, old value, new value, event ID, evidence.
R23: Sort by residual score (highest first); for equal scores, higher inherent score first. Trend: score went up ↑, down ↓, no change →. "So what" frame: "If this happens, <consequence copied from the statement>." Risk for acceptance = the Medium risk with the highest residual score (equal scores: lowest Risk ID). Expiry = today + 12 months; re-assessment = expiry − 30 days; approver = rule R36.
R24: Class 1: KEV-listed or Critical on an internet-facing asset → 7 days. Class 2: Critical, or KEV on an internal asset → 14 days. Class 3: High → 30 days. Class 4: Medium → 90 days. Due = first detected + SLA. Exception valid only if approved by system owner AND CISO, has a compensating control, and has not expired.
R25: Write three recommendations: the Ref-Actions action for the three classes (or deviation types) with the most breaches, in that order.
R26: High = affects a Mission Critical system or no evidence exists. Medium = done late or partly. Low = record-keeping only.
R27: Use the tier from rule R35. Then include every question in Ref-Questions marked for that tier or a lower tier. Clause checklist: include every clause marked for the tier; add "transfer mechanism" if data leaves the country.
R28: Check S1–S9 (Ref-SOC checks). Reject if S4 (qualified opinion) or S9 (service not in scope). Otherwise Approve with conditions if any S-check fails (one condition per failed check from Ref-Conditions, due in 90 days). Approve if none fails.
R29: Role = the value in the dataset column "Role (contract register)". DPIA required = Yes if the activity involves any of: children or students, AI/analytics/profiling, monitoring or recording, health data, identity checks (KYC/AML). Otherwise No.
R30: For every affected office and every data-subject country, look up the regimes in addendum §2. Deadline = discovery time (UTC) + clock. Mark the earliest firm deadline. Tell data subjects = Yes if the data includes children's data, health data, financial data or credentials, or more than 1,000 people; otherwise No.
R31: Use the 4-week template: Week 1 lesson, Week 2 poster + quiz, Week 3 phishing simulation, Week 4 results + refresher. Copy the scenario card and the 3 behaviours for your theme from Ref-Content. Approvals: HR + Legal always; add works council where addendum §2 lists one for the office.
R32: Copy the obligations from the official source (steps in T11.2). Applicability per office: rule R02. Affected policies: use the keyword table in Ref-Keywords. Action due date = publication date + 30 days.
R33: An action is "Closed — verified" only if all are true: closure evidence is attached (else K1); it is dated after the action was raised (else K2); it is a system record, not a statement (else K3); the re-test passed (else K4). Otherwise the status is "Open" with the failed code. An open action more than 14 days past its due date and not yet escalated → escalate to the owner's manager (K5). Next check date = test date + 14 days.
R34: Answer each request with ONE evidence file: same control or clause, dated inside the audit period, from a system (not an undated screenshot). Record file ID and SHA-256. If no file matches, answer "No evidence available" and raise an action (never create evidence after the request). For a finding: open the named evidence file — if it shows the problem, accept and state the corrective action; if it shows the control worked, challenge with the row; if still disputed, name the route (closing meeting, then the certification body's appeal process).
R35: Critical: access to Tier 4 data or children's data at scale, OR a customer-facing or regulatory-critical service that is hard to replace. High: access to Tier 3 personal/confidential data at volume, OR a revenue-critical service. Medium: limited personal data or pseudonymous data, easy to replace. Low: only public/anonymous data. Check from Critical down; stop at the first match.
R36: Low → Risk owner. Medium → Org CRCO. High → Org CEO + Group CISO. Critical → Not acceptable (Board decision). Source: Charter §6.1. Always use this table, even if the register shows a different value.
L01: Clauses 4, 5, 6, 7 → Plan; clause 8 → Do; clause 9 → Check; clause 10 → Act (conventional mapping).
L02: Requirements = ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27006-1, ISO/IEC 17021-1. All other listed documents = guidance.
L03: In scope = the office(s) and departments of your organisation in the asset register. Out of scope = only the items listed as "excluded" in the addendum, with the addendum reason. Interfaces = the first 3 external rows of the TSA Integrations sheet. Climate change relevant = Yes (Group decision, BKB-POL-015); copy the Group reason from the sheet Ref-ISMS processes.
L04: Copy the 10 ISMS processes and owners from Ref-ISMS processes (Learn › Reference) (the Group RACI in the Charter: risk assessment, SoA, document control, competence, awareness, incident, supplier, internal audit, management review, corrective action).
L05: Copy the control type, security property and cybersecurity concept for the control from Ref-27002 attributes (Learn › Reference).
L06: Every control is Applicable. A control is Not applicable only if it appears in Ref-SoA exclusions (Learn › Reference); copy the justification shown there. Justification for applicable controls: copy the first source found in this order — risk register treatment ID, law in addendum §2, contract in Organization_Profiles, "Group baseline (BKB-POL-001)".
L07: Look up the control in the TSA Control_Mapping sheet. Product listed → "Yes". Listed in the Roadmap sheet only → "Planned". Not listed → "No".
L08: For each of the 7 items, search BKB-POL-001 for the key word in the template. Found → copy the section number. Not found → "Gap".
L09: Copy the RACI from the Charter table for the 10 ISMS processes (rule L04). Do not change any letter.
L10: Copy the 14 rows from the template; for each, write the BKB library location from Ref-Locations (Learn › Reference).
L11: Copy from Ref-Certification card (Learn › Reference): Stage 1 = documents and readiness; Stage 2 = implementation on site; surveillance in years 2 and 3; recertification before year 3 ends. Certification-body criteria = the 5 listed on the card, in order.
L12: Residual score > 11 → "Modify". Residual score ≤ 11 → "Retain". Controls = the SoA controls listed for the risk category in Ref-Keywords.
L13: For each clause look up your deliverable in Ref-Clause map (Learn › Reference). Deliverable submitted and accepted → "Conforms". Submitted with review comments → "Partial". Not in the list → "Gap".
L14: Copy the 3 objective templates from the sheet Ref-Objectives. Fill the numbers: leavers disabled within 4 h (target 95 %), critical vulnerabilities fixed within SLA (target 90 %), staff trained (target 95 %). Owner and date from the template.
L15: Copy the 6 fixed milestones from the sheet Ref-Milestones (scope approved → SoA approved → controls implemented → internal audit → management review → Stage 1). Start = programme week 12 + 1 month; each milestone lasts 1 month. Owner = RACI "A" for that process.
L16: Copy the 10 field names from the sheet Ref-Measure card. Fill each field from your VUL-TEST (formula, numbers) and the fixed values on that sheet (frequency monthly, analysed by GRC team, evaluated by CISO, reported to management review).
L17: Major = the required activity was never done in the period OR failed in more than half of the sample. Minor = any other failure.
L18: Answer the 5 fixed questions on the form (sheet Ref-5-Whys) by copying facts from your test evidence. The last answer is the root cause. Correction = the Ref-Actions action for the instance. Corrective action = "Add the missing step to the procedure and train the owners". Effectiveness check = re-test 3 months later.
L19: Copy the service model from the vendor intake form. Copy the responsibility table for that model from the sheet Ref-Cloud. Add the 5 fixed cloud and supply-chain questions from the same sheet.
L20: Phases: plan (A.5.24), detect and report, assess and decide (A.5.25), respond (A.5.26), learn (A.5.27); evidence A.5.28. Invoke the DR plan if a Mission Critical system is unavailable longer than its RTO. Invoke the BC plan if a critical process has stopped longer than its RTO. Otherwise "Not invoked".
L21: Copy the competence rows for the 3 roles named in the template from the sheet Ref-Competence. Copy the 6 fixed ISMS communications from the sheet Ref-Communications and fill the date column from the programme calendar.
L22: Tick each ISMS element the sheet Ref-Change types lists for the topic type. Place each affected system on the layer shown in the TSA Technology_Stack "Domain" column.
L23: Year 1: clauses 4–10 + Annex A organisational; Year 2: people + physical; Year 3: technological. Auditor = Internal Audit (never the process owner). Frequency: controls with open or repeat actions in T12.1 are audited every year.
L24: Fill one row per 9.3.2 input (a–g) from the sheet Ref-Review inputs (it names the deliverable for each input). Stage 1 ready = Yes only if all 14 mandatory documents in LI-DOC are "Present"; otherwise No and list the missing ones.
L25: Open the evidence file named in the finding. If the row shows the problem → say "I accept" and read the Ref-Actions action. If the row does not show the problem → read the row and say "The evidence shows ___". Then say the route: closing meeting, then the certification body's appeal process.

Effective: no exceptions in the sample or in full-population analytics. Effective with exceptions: only Low/Medium exceptions and the total number of exceptions ≤ 5 % of the population. Not effective: any High-severity exception, or exceptions > 5 % of the population. (Control tests T8.2: 1–2 deviations = effective with exceptions; > 2 = not effective.)

Policy class: (1) KEV-listed OR Critical (CVSS ≥ 9.0) on an internet-facing asset → 7 days; (2) Critical, or KEV-listed on an internal asset → 14 days; (3) High (7.0–8.9) → 30 days; (4) Medium (4.0–6.9) → 90 days. Due = first detected + SLA. A valid exception is approved by system owner + CISO, has a compensating control and has not expired at the test date.

Critical: access to Tier 4 data or children's data at scale, OR customer-facing/regulatory-critical service that is hard to substitute. High: access to Tier 3 personal/confidential data at volume, OR revenue-critical service. Medium: limited personal data or pseudonymous data, easy substitution. Low: no access to Group information beyond public/anonymous data.

F1.1: What will I do
Your first day in the Group GRC Office. Complete onboarding: confirm your assignment, accept the conduct rules, set your hours and make your first recorded submission.
Why am I doing this

Every GRC job starts with conduct: you handle other people's data and you produce records that auditors rely on. Before you touch any task, the organisation needs proof that you know the rules (BKB-POL-024 §6.1) and that your workspace records your work correctly.
What will I learn
Follow the mentee conduct and data rules — synthetic data only, own work, no AI tools for task work — see BKB-POL-024 §3.1; BKB-POL-022 §7.1
Recognise what a controlled record looks like: hash, UTC time, version, naming convention — see Capture standard — BKB-MEN-101 §9
Use the scripted help: the "In simpler words" note on every step, the glossary and the "Report a problem" form — see Guided Model — principle G7
Plan your own working hours so that reminders and task messages reach you — see Guided Model — "My schedule"

See which areas of the GRC capability this task practises — U3 Culture and conduct; D1 Mandate, leadership and resources; O6 Speak-up channels and investigation — and what your deliverables evidence — see Ref-Capability map (Learn › Reference pages)
How to do it

6 numbered steps, of which 3 are decisions from options (judgement share 50 %). Rules you will use: copy and calculation only (Learn › Rule tables). Assigned by the Cybersecurity Program Manager, who has written the "In simpler words" note on every step. Help is pre-written on the platform (no live chat).

A corrective action removes the cause; a correction fixes one case (decision T8.2-D6). Final Exam items I49 and I50. PECB LI domain(s) 5, 6, 7; ISO/IEC 27001 10.2; 10.1.

Cloud and ICT supply-chain controls (A.5.21, A.5.23) need the service model and the responsibility split before any question is useful.
Identify IaaS / PaaS / SaaS, state who secures what, add the fixed cloud and supply-chain questions — see Rule L19; Ref-Cloud; BKB-POL-021
3 steps inside task T9.1 (marked [LI-13]). Rules: L19. Adds 0.5 h.

In SaaS the provider patches the platform but the customer still owns identities and data classification — questions aimed at the wrong party get useless answers. PECB LI domain(s) 2, 4; ISO/IEC 27001 A.5.21, A.5.23.
LI-14: Incident-management process and business continuity vs disaster recovery: Map incident INC-2610-3001 to the incident phases and decide BC/DR invocation (L20).

Incident management is a life-cycle (A.5.24–A.5.28); continuity and disaster recovery are different plans (A.5.29–A.5.30). Knowing which to invoke, and when, is the implementer's call in the first hours.
Map an incident to the five phases with their Annex A controls and apply the BC/DR invocation rule — see Rule L20; ISO/IEC 27035-1; BKB-POL-014; BKB-POL-015
4 steps inside task T10.2 (marked [LI-14]). Rules: L20. Adds 1.0 h.
Platform: Regulatory Watch › Breach Clock Calculator. Template: T-LI-IRBC. GRC record: Incident life-cycle note — attached to the notification plan (T10.2).
LI-IRBC — Incident life-cycle and continuity decision (DOCX 1 page)

BC keeps the business running; DR restores ICT. Invoke DR when a Mission Critical system is down longer than its RTO (L20). HC5 reviews the judgement. PECB LI domain(s) 4; ISO/IEC 27001 A.5.24–A.5.30.
LI-15: Competence, awareness and ISMS communication plan: Plan competence and ISMS communication (L21).
Clauses 7.2–7.4 require competence with evidence, awareness and a communication plan — the people side of the ISMS, not only the technical side.
Build a competence matrix for three ISMS roles and a communication plan answering what, when, with whom, how, who — see Rule L21; Ref-Competence; ISO/IEC 27001 cl. 7.2–7.4
4 steps inside task T11.1 (marked [LI-15]). Rules: L21. Adds 1.5 h.
Platform: Awareness › Content Templates. Template: T-LI-COMM. GRC record: Competence matrix and communication plan — evidence of competence (7.2) for the management review.

Clause 7.2 needs action AND evidence of competence (decision T11.1-D4). Top management, not an intern, announces the policy (cl. 5.1, 7.4). PECB LI domain(s) 4; ISO/IEC 27001 7.2, 7.3, 7.4.
LI-16: Planning changes to the ISMS, new technology and architecture impact: Record the ISMS impact of "EU Digital Services Act guidelines on the protection of minors online (2025)" (L22).
Clause 6.3 says changes to the ISMS must be planned. A regulatory change can touch scope, risks, SoA, objectives, documents and resources; the architecture view shows which systems are hit.
Record the ISMS elements a change affects, place systems on the BKB-TECH-000 layers and assess new-technology impact — see Rule L22; Ref-Change types; ISO/IEC 27001 cl. 6.3; A.5.8, A.8.27
5 steps inside task T11.2 (marked [LI-16]). Rules: L22. Adds 1.0 h.
Platform: Regulatory Watch › Impact Log. Template: T-LI-CHG. GRC record: ISMS change-impact note — attached to the regulatory brief (T11.2).
LI-CHG — ISMS change impact note (DOCX 1 page)
Unplanned ISMS change is how scope statements and SoAs go stale between audits. Final Exam item I56 (big data, AI, cloud). PECB LI domain(s) 2, 4, 6; ISO/IEC 27001 6.3; A.5.8, A.8.27.
LI-17: Internal audit programme, management review pack and certification readiness: Prepare the audit programme, management-review pack and Stage 1 readiness (L23, L24).
Clauses 9.2 and 9.3 require a risk-based internal audit programme and a management review with defined inputs and outputs; readiness for Stage 1 is a yes/no decision with reasons.
Plan a 3-year audit programme with independence, build the 9.3.2 a–g review pack and give an evidenced readiness verdict — see Rules L23, L24; Ref-Review inputs; ISO/IEC 27007
5 steps inside task T12.1 (marked [LI-17]). Rules: L23, L24. Adds 2.0 h.

Nobody audits their own work (decision T12.1-D6). Stage 1 is "ready" only if every mandatory document in LI-DOC is present (L24). HC6 checks that the verdict is honest. PECB LI domain(s) 5, 6, 7; ISO/IEC 27001 9.2.2, 9.3.2, 9.3.3, 10.1.
LI-18: Challenging an external audit finding: Add the requirement and the appeal route to your NC-1 response (L25).
Findings are only valid against a stated requirement. A professional auditee quotes the clause, shows the evidence, and knows the appeal route.
Respond to NC-1 by quoting the requirement, citing the evidence row and naming the escalation route — see Rule L25; ISO/IEC 17021-1 (appeals)
4 steps inside task T12.2 (marked [LI-18]). Rules: L25. Adds 0.5 h.

Refusing to sign or deleting a finding is never the route (decision T12.2-D6); the certification body's appeal process is. PECB LI domain(s) 6, 7; ISO/IEC 27001 10.2; ISO/IEC 17021-1 (appeals).

principles: G1
Half instructions, half decisions
About 50 % of every task's activities are decisions made from options provided; the rest are numbered instruction steps. Each task shows its judgement share.
G2
Decisions use provided options
The mentee never writes an opinion from nothing: each decision offers fixed options (A/B/C, or a drop-down per row). The rules in Ref-Rules tell the mentee how to choose.
G3
Feedback after every decision
After submission the mentee sees the best option and a one-line reason. Wrong choices are learning points, not penalties beyond the scoring weight.
G4
Fixed templates and sentence frames
Outputs are templates with drop-down lists. Where text is needed, the mentee completes a sentence frame. Free writing is not assessed.
G5
Plain English
Short sentences, common words, one action per step (CEFR level B1). A glossary explains every GRC term. English style is never scored.
G9
Foundation weeks: less is more

Weeks 1–2 teach one rule per task with a worked example before every decision type: no risk assessment, no Lead Implementer extension, at most six steps and three decisions per task, at most eight hours per week, one scripted message per task.
G6
Task messages carry a learning point

Each task sends scripted messages (one in the Foundation weeks, two from week 3): a situation to decide (A/B/C) and either an extra data file or a data-handling decision. Each ends with why it matters.
G7
Help is scripted, never a chat

There is no agent or person to chat with. Every step carries a pre-written "In simpler words" note and names its rule; the Learn section holds the glossary and the rule tables; "Report a problem" is a form answered by the programme office. Nothing on the platform gives the answer to a decision.
G8
Reviews check decisions and evidence
AI and human reviewers score decision accuracy against the key, correct rule application, evidence for every row, and data handling.

principles: One workspace per mentee on the GRCMentorship platform, provisioned at onboarding (BKB-POL-024 §6.1 step 3). Nothing is submitted by e-mail or chat.
Everything the mentee does is captured as a record: artefacts, a structured work log, an evidence trail, task-message responses and problem reports.
Synthetic data only: every dataset is generated by the assignment engine; mentees never handle live, production or real personal data (BKB-POL-024 §3.1; BKB-STD-001 handling matrix "Mentee use").
Records are immutable once submitted: each submission gets a SHA-256 hash, a UTC timestamp and a version number; resubmission creates a new version and never overwrites.
Evidence-quality rules that mentees learn in Week 2 (BKB-POL-016 §7.1: dated, attributable, complete for the period, unaltered) apply to their own work.
The mentee ticks each instruction step, records each decision (option chosen) and the rule used; the platform records the rest automatically.
folders: Undertaking, privacy-notice acknowledgement, data and AI rules acknowledgement, weekly schedule
Read-only: dataset(s), instructions and the library task anchor issued by the engine
Drafts and scratch files (not assessed; retained for integrity checks)
Task messages received and the steps ticked (INJECT_LOG)
Automated review record, assessor review record, moderation and re-check records (read-only to mentee)
Knowledge checks, Foundation Gate Exam, Final Exam forms and results
Auto-compiled portfolio of all submitted work and final transcript
worklog: Step number — set when the mentee ticks the step as done
The step text (copied by the platform)
For decision steps: option chosen (A/B/C or per-row value) — compared with the key after submission
Rule ID used in the step (R01–R36, L01–L25) or "copy" / "calculation"
Document and section or dataset row ID used (e.g., BKB-POL-006 §6.2; UAR row U-0142)
Yes/No — the scripted "In simpler words" note was opened for this step (never penalised)
Minutes between step start and tick
Link to a "Report a problem" form sent from this step, if any
capture.evidence_trail: Every finding, rating or mapping in a submission must cite the dataset row ID(s) or document clause it rests on in a column named "Evidence ref". The automated review rejects findings without an evidence reference.
capture.retention: Mentee records are retained for 3 years after programme completion under a dedicated privacy notice (BKB-POL-024 §3.1), then deleted.
late: Due dates are set by the system; the deadline is 23:59 on the due day (mentee's time zone).
Late submission: −10 % of the task score per started 24 hours, for up to 72 hours; after 72 hours the task scores 0 but must still be submitted to count towards completion.
One grace period per programme: the system automatically applies a 48-hour extension without penalty to the first late task.
Task messages are answered within 2 working days and scored 0–4 on the task-message rubric.
Moderation: when the AI and human scores for the same deliverable differ by more than 15 points, a Moderator third-marks it blind; the moderated score replaces both (BKB-POL-024 §6.2 step 3).

Re-checks are automatic: every task scored below 65 and every final result below Pass is re-checked by a Moderator before it is released; no action is needed from the mentee. A mentee may still ask for a re-check with the "Request re-check" form (a right, not a task).
schedule: In F1.1 the mentee sets their working hours per weekday in "My schedule" (at least 12 hours a week on at least 3 days; at most 4 hours in one sitting).
Reminders and task messages are sent during those hours, so the mentee is never contacted while offline. Due dates are fixed by the programme calendar.
Next week's hours can be changed until Friday 23:59 (own time zone). Due dates stay the same.
If the mentee is inactive for a full week of set hours, the programme office makes a welfare check.

items: Weekly knowledge checks: 10 questions, 15 minutes, open book, two attempts (new form each time).
Foundation Gate Exam at the end of week 2: 30 questions, 45 minutes, pass mark 70 % (one resit).
Performance tasks: the extracts you receive contain planted problems. The rules find them when you apply them step by step.
Decisions: about half of every task; scored against the answer key (best option per situation or per row).
Task messages: one per task in weeks 1–2, two per task from week 3; a situation to decide and an extra data file or data-handling decision.
Final Exam in week 12: 40 questions (60 min) plus a 30-minute practical — a 60-row access extract with 8 hidden exceptions.
gates: Foundation Gate Exam ≥ 70 % (one resit on a new form within 5 working days; a failed resit defers the mentee to the next cohort).
At least 22 of 25 tasks submitted (≥ 85 % — the Charter KPI for task completion).

No confirmed integrity breach (use of live/real data, copying another mentee's work, impersonation, or use of any AI tool for task work — the platform has no chat assistant; all help is scripted). A confirmed breach is an automatic fail and is reported to the Programme Quality Lead.

Accuracy and decisions against the answer key
Decision points: best option chosen (per scenario, per row for item decisions). Planted defects found, no false findings, calculations correct within tolerance.
Every finding has an evidence reference (row ID or clause); references are real and correctly cited.
Template unchanged, naming convention, manifest, steps ticked and rule IDs recorded.
Submitted by the system due date; task messages answered within 2 working days.
hcrit: Choices match the key; where a choice differs, the rule and evidence cited show a reasonable reading. Patterns of wrong choices become coaching points.
Every value has a source (document + section, or dataset row) in the "Evidence ref" column.
Instruction steps done; rules applied as written; templates and frames used as issued; task messages answered.
Accuracy and completeness of the record
Values copied exactly; calculations correct; no empty required field.
Only workspace data used; drills reported; own work; nothing sent outside the platform.
bands: and no composite below 75; digital badge "GRC 101 — Distinction"
remediation path: repeat up to 4 failed weeks in the next cohort with newly generated, unique tasks (once)

Rules R11–R13 applied correctly; look-ups complete; redlines follow the frame; fix location (Group or Addendum) correct. ISO/IEC 27001 LI extensions: LI-05 — L06/L07 applied exactly; every justification has a source. LI-06 — L08/L09 applied exactly.

Rules R28 and R30 applied correctly; every deadline traceable to an addendum row; legal sign-off box ticked. ISO/IEC 27001 LI extensions: LI-14 — L20 applied correctly.

Rules R33 and R34 applied correctly; closure decisions and escalations justified by the evidence; right evidence file for each auditor request; response to the finding follows the evidence. ISO/IEC 27001 LI extensions: LI-17 — L23/L24 applied correctly; readiness verdict follows the rule. LI-18 — clause quoted; response follows the evidence.
inject_format: Situation — one or two short sentences from the current task (plain English).
Options — A, B, C (DECISION and DRILL), or numbered steps for an extra data file (DATA).
Learning point — shown after answering: the best option and why it matters.
Read — the rule or document that guides the choice.
inject_rubric: DECISION/DRILL: best option chosen. DATA: rows added and rules applied correctly.
DECISION: a defensible but weaker option (named in the key). DATA: rows added with one error.
Answered late (after 2 working days) or DATA incomplete.
Not answered, wrong option, OR (DRILL) the offered data was accepted or forwarded.

Scores Human Checkpoints HC1–HC6; gives written feed-forward; flags integrity concerns. Ratio 1 : 35 mentees.
Senior assessor who has passed calibration with ≥ 0.75 agreement for two consecutive months.

Cybersecurity Program Manager (policy owner of BKB-POL-024) or delegate.

F1.1: Open Home › My Organisation

You are already on the platform — this is your workplace for the next 12 weeks. "My Organisation" is your assignment: the two organisations you support, their offices, the person (role) who assigns each task and your start date. You will see these names in every task. Nothing to decide here — read, then tick the step.
do
Decide: A colleague asks for your login so they can finish a step f…

First a scripted question with three options. Think about who owns your account. Choose one option; the platform shows the best option and why after you submit the task. Then open the undertaking, read it and sign it — your signature is the record that you know the rules.
pick
Decide: You do not understand a rule. What do you use

Again one scripted question. The point: all help on this platform is pre-written — the note you are reading now, the glossary in Learn, the rule tables under Learn › Rule tables. No AI tool and no chat is used for task work. Then tick every box of the data rules.
pick
Decide: You can work 15 hours a week

Choose the schedule that follows the three numbers: at least 12 hours a week, on at least 3 days, never more than 4 hours in one sitting. Then enter your own hours in "My schedule" — reminders and task messages arrive only inside those hours.
pick
Open the file READ-ME-FIRST in your task folder (01_Inputs)

Your first real submission, the way every deliverable works: a file goes from 01_Inputs (what you receive) through 02_Working (your work) to Submit. The receipt shows a hash (a fingerprint of the file) and a UTC time. If the hash is missing, use "Report a problem".
do
Open "My plan"
"My plan" lists every due date of the 12 weeks. The system set them inside your working hours. You do not change anything — this step only shows you where to look. Then click "Done".
do
F1.2: Open template T-FAM

The template already lists every standard of both organisations with the Mandatory/Optional flag copied from the addendum §3. The rows of your second organisation are complete — they are your worked examples. Read five of them before you start.
do
Read the worked example in row 1: "ISO/IEC 27001:2022 — Can an organi…

Row 1 shows how rule R01 is applied: ask the questions in order and stop at the first "yes". ISO/IEC 27001 — can an organisation get a certificate? Yes → certifiable standard. Every row works the same way.
do
Decide for each row: For each standard of GlobalConnect Customer Solutions, deci…

Now your rows. For each standard of your first organisation ask the R01 questions in this order: made by a parliament or regulator? certificate possible? auditor's report? contract wording? otherwise voluntary. Select the type from the drop-down and write "R01" in the Rule column. Scored per row.
each
Decide: A standard is named only in the row for one regional office…

A scripted question first, then a copy step. Rule R02: a standard applies to an office when the addendum §2 row of that office names it. Open §2, find the office rows, copy the office names next to every mandatory standard.
pick
Decide: Which "Evidence ref" is acceptable

A source is something another person can open and check: the document name and the section. "My notes" and "Internet" are not sources. Write the addendum and §3 in the Evidence ref column of every row.
pick
Submit FAM-MAP. Click "Done".
Press Submit. The platform seals the file (hash + UTC time) and starts the automated review. You can reopen a step before you submit, not after.
